question: Should OpenClaw accept Android device-control, ADB-style access, or dynamic code execution from connected Android nodes, and should the execution-oriented pieces be Android-specific commands or wait for the generic node-hosted tool contract?
rationale: The remaining work changes phone authority, private-data access, and model-visible execution boundaries, so automation cannot choose the permanent product and security shape.

options.title: Split And Gate Android Authority
options.body: Implement only narrow permission-gated device-control commands after explicit permission UX and policy review, while deferring ADB and dynamic execution until the generic node-tool trust model is accepted.

options.title: Route Through Node-Hosted Tools
options.body: Use the #8287 and #90431 design path as the core contract, then let Android expose only approved descriptors through that generic model.

options.title: Reject High-Power Core Execution
options.body: Keep ADB and dynamic Android code execution out of OpenClaw core for now and require external plugins or app-specific forks for that authority.

recommendation.title: Split And Gate Android Authority
recommendation.body: Implement only narrow permission-gated device-control commands after explicit permission UX and policy review, while deferring ADB and dynamic execution until the generic node-tool trust model is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current signal for the generic node-to-model tool contract is the open node-hosted plugin tools path under this account.
